skill.name: pixijs-core-concepts
skill.description: Use this skill when understanding how PixiJS v8 renders frames: the systems-and-pipes renderer, the render loop, and how the library adapts to different environments. Covers WebGLRenderer/WebGPURenderer/CanvasRenderer selection, renderer.render() pipeline, environment detection, rendering into RenderTextures and RenderTargets (flipY, mipLevel, layer, bind/push/pop, copyDepthTexture), WebGL context loss and WebGPU device loss recovery, and pointers to per-topic deep dives. Triggers on: renderer, WebGL, WebGPU, Canvas, render loop, render pipeline, systems, environments, autoDetectRenderer, RenderTexture, RenderTarget, render to texture, flipY, mipLevel, layer, 3D texture, depth slice, renderTarget.bind, copyToTexture, copyDepthTexture, depth-only, WebGLLoader, WebGPULoader, CanvasLoader, RendererLoader, lazy-load renderer systems, code splitting, context lost, webglcontextlost, device lost, GPUDevice.lost.
skill.summary: Understand PixiJS v8 renderer selection, frame execution, render targets, and environment integration.
skill.author: pixijs

content.user_title: Understand PixiJS v8 Rendering and Frame Loops
content.value_statement: Renderer selection and frame timing can make PixiJS applications difficult to debug. This skill explains backend selection, rendering architecture, and frame execution with focused examples.
actual_capabilities: Explain renderer preference strings, ordered backend arrays, fallback behavior, and runtime backend checks.
Describe renderer systems, render pipes, and backend-specific loader extensions for lazy loading.
Explain ticker callback priorities, time units, frame rate limits, and manual rendering patterns.
Guide rendering into textures and targets with mip levels, layers, depth attachments, and orientation options.
Describe WebGL context restoration, WebGPU device loss, and render bundle validity checks.
Identify initialization order mistakes and explain when environment adapters must be configured.
limitations: Provides documentation and examples, not an executable renderer, automated test suite, or benchmark tool.
Targets PixiJS v8; API details can differ between installed releases.
Full application setup, custom rendering implementations, and environment configuration rely on separate skills.
Does not guarantee browser backend availability or Canvas feature parity with GPU renderers.

use_cases.description: Compare backend preferences, fallback rules, and feature checks before selecting rendering options for a browser application.

use_cases.title: Coordinate physics and animation
use_cases.description: Order simulation callbacks before drawing and select appropriate ticker time units for game updates.

use_cases.title: Integrate custom render targets

prompt_templates.title: Explain the rendering model
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how PixiJS v8 selects a renderer and draws a frame. Describe systems, render pipes, and the ticker in simple terms.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a backend preference
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare a WebGPU preference string with a WebGPU and WebGL preference array. Explain fallback behavior and checking the selected renderer after initialization.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose frame timing
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my PixiJS v8 ticker callbacks below. Identify priority or time-unit mistakes and explain how to run physics before rendering: [callbacks].

prompt_templates.title: Plan offscreen rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a PixiJS v8 offscreen rendering workflow with depth copying and backend-specific lazy loaders. Explain target lifecycle, device loss recovery, and version-sensitive assumptions.

output_examples.input: Why does preferring WebGPU still produce a WebGL renderer?
output: A preference string tries the requested backend and can continue through fallback choices.
An ordered preference array limits selection to the listed backends.
Inspect the renderer name after initialization before using backend-specific features.

output_examples.input: How should I order physics, animation, rendering, and pixel readback?
output: Run physics callbacks at HIGH priority and ordinary animation callbacks at NORMAL priority.
The application render callback runs at LOW priority.
Schedule pixel readback at UTILITY priority after rendering.
Use deltaMS for millisecond-based updates and deltaTime for normalized frame multipliers.

output_examples.input: What should I check before copying depth between render targets?
output: Use WebGL2 or WebGPU and a destination texture with a depth format.
Clear only color on the next destination render to preserve copied depth.
Balance target push and pop operations, and destroy targets when they are no longer needed.

best_practices: Configure environment adapters before initialization, then await initialization before accessing renderer resources.
Check the selected backend before using backend-specific features and verify examples against your installed PixiJS release.
Assign explicit callback priorities and choose time units that match your simulation calculations.
anti_patterns: Assuming a WebGPU preference guarantees WebGPU support on every browser.
Combining an automatic rendering loop with redundant manual rendering calls.
Expecting Canvas to support GPU filters, compressed textures, and custom shaders.

faq.question: Which PixiJS version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers PixiJS v8. Check your installed release because newer renderer and render target APIs may not exist in earlier versions.

faq.question: Can I use this skill with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. It supplies reference guidance rather than a standalone application.

faq.question: Does this skill install or run PixiJS?
faq.answer: No. The package contains Markdown guidance and TypeScript examples, not an installer or runnable project.

faq.question: How do I identify the active renderer?
faq.answer: Await application initialization, then inspect app.renderer.name. Use that value before calling backend-specific features.

faq.question: Does this skill include complete Worker or SSR setup?
faq.answer: It explains adapter timing and points to the separate pixijs-environments skill for complete Worker, SSR, and strict CSP configuration.

faq.question: Are the static security warnings evidence of malicious behavior?
faq.answer: No evidence found of malicious behavior. The reviewed matches are documentation formatting, a fixed local import example, renderer identification, and API reference links.
